# Question and experimental design

Does supplemental inter-row weed management affect the amount of cereal rye
mulch remaining at peak weed sampling? The primary planned comparison is
inter-row mowing (RIM) versus rolled rye with no supplemental management (RNO).
High-residue cultivation (RIC) versus RNO is a secondary planned comparison.

Only the three rolled treatments have mulch measurements. Total mulch biomass
was measured in 2023 Field V, 2024 O2 East, and 2024 O2 West, with four
randomized blocks per site-year. Each plot contributes one independent
observation (3 site-years × 4 blocks × 3 treatments = 36 plots). The response
is **remaining mulch biomass**, not a direct pre/post estimate of biomass
removed by an operation.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(WrensBookshelf)
```

# Import and prepare data

Set `data_path` to the location of the processed dataset in your Mowtivation
repository if none of these common locations applies. The analysis uses the
already converted `mulch_biomass_kg_ha` field, so no second unit conversion
is performed.

```{r import}
candidate_paths <- c(
  here("data", "processed", "combined_processed.rds"),
  here("data", "combined_processed.rds"),
  here("combined_processed.rds"),
  here("upload", "combined_processed(2).rds")
)
existing_paths <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)]
if (length(existing_paths) == 0) {
  stop("Cannot find combined_processed.rds. Set data_path to its location.")
}
data_path <- existing_paths[1]
combined <- readRDS(data_path)

mulch <- combined |>
  filter(as.character(treatment) %in% c("RNO", "RIM", "RIC")) |>
  transmute(
    site_year = factor(as.character(site_year),
                       levels = c("V_2023", "O2E_2024", "O2W_2024"),
                       labels = c("2023 Field V", "2024 O2 East", "2024 O2 West")),
    block = factor(block),
    treatment = factor(as.character(treatment), levels = c("RNO", "RIM", "RIC")),
    mulch_kg_ha = as.numeric(mulch_biomass_kg_ha)
  )

stopifnot(nrow(mulch) == 36, !anyNA(mulch),
          all(mulch$mulch_kg_ha > 0),
          all(as.vector(table(mulch$site_year, mulch$treatment)) == 4),
          all(as.vector(table(mulch$site_year, mulch$block)) == 3))

mulch |> count(site_year, treatment)
```

# Descriptive summaries

The tables and figures below show **observed plot means ± standard errors**.
They are not model-adjusted estimates. With a balanced design, each site-year
contributes equally to the overall treatment means.

```{r summaries}
summary_by_site <- mulch |>
  group_by(site_year, treatment) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(mulch_kg_ha),
            sd = sd(mulch_kg_ha), se = sd / sqrt(n), .groups = "drop")

summary_overall <- mulch |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(mulch_kg_ha),
            sd = sd(mulch_kg_ha), se = sd / sqrt(n), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(summary_by_site, digits = 1)
knitr::kable(summary_overall, digits = 1)
```

The across-site-year raw SE above includes between-site-year variability.
Because treatment was randomized *within* site-year and block, that SE is
descriptive and should not be used to test treatment differences. Inference
comes from the blocked model below.

# Fit the primary model

Site-year and treatment are fixed effects, including their interaction; block
nested in site-year is a random intercept. We retain the interaction to assess
whether mowing effects vary by site-year. We start with a Gaussian model on
the original kg/ha scale and inspect its assumptions rather than assuming a
transformation is needed.

```{r model}
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
mulch_model <- lmer(
  mulch_kg_ha ~ site_year * treatment + (1 | site_year:block),
  data = mulch, REML = TRUE
)

summary(mulch_model)
anova(mulch_model, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite")
```

# Model diagnostics

Inspect the residual-versus-fitted plot for changing variance or systematic
patterns, and the Q-Q plot for substantial departures from normality. Site-year
residual spreads are also summarized. If serious heterogeneity appears, revisit
the residual variance structure before drawing conclusions.

```{r diagnostics, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
diagnostics <- tibble(
  fitted = fitted(mulch_model),
  residual = resid(mulch_model),
  site_year = mulch$site_year
)

p_resid <- ggplot(diagnostics, aes(fitted, residual, color = site_year)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Fitted mulch biomass (kg/ha)", y = "Residual (kg/ha)", color = "Site-year") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

p_qq <- ggplot(diagnostics, aes(sample = residual)) +
  stat_qq(size = 2) + stat_qq_line() +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample residual quantiles") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

print(p_resid)
print(p_qq)

diagnostics |> group_by(site_year) |>
  summarise(residual_sd = sd(residual), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Planned treatment comparisons

The main inferential question is **RIM − RNO** averaged equally over the three
site-years. We also report RIC − RNO, adjusting these two control comparisons
using Dunnett's method. A negative difference means less remaining mulch than
RNO. If the treatment × site-year interaction is important, interpret the
site-year-specific differences alongside (or instead of) the pooled average.

```{r contrasts}
emm_treatment <- emmeans(mulch_model, ~ treatment, weights = "equal")
planned_vs_rno <- contrast(emm_treatment, method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1)
summary(planned_vs_rno, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), adjust = "dunnettx")

```

# Figures: raw means ± SE

The overall treatment test is nonsignificant, so no exploratory Fisher's LSD
post-hoc grouping or CLD letters are shown. The prespecified comparisons
against RNO above address the mowing and cultivation questions directly and
do not require a significant omnibus treatment test. Figure means and error
bars are descriptive; statistical inference uses the blocked mixed model.

```{r figure-data}
treatment_codes <- c("RNO", "RIM", "RIC", "TIM", "TIC")
treatment_colors <- setNames(
  WrensBookshelf::WB_brewer(name = "WhatWellBuild", n = 5, type = "discrete"),
  treatment_codes
)
rolled_colors <- treatment_colors[c("RNO", "RIM", "RIC")]
rolled_labels <- c("RNO" = "Rolled only", "RIM" = "Inter-row mowing",
                   "RIC" = "High-residue cultivation")
```

```{r overall-figure, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
mulch_overall_fig <- ggplot(summary_overall, aes(treatment, mean, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
                width = 0.16, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rolled_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = rolled_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
  labs(x = "Rolled rye treatment", y = "Remaining mulch biomass (kg/ha)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 13))

mulch_overall_fig
```

```{r site-year-figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
mulch_site_year_fig <- ggplot(summary_by_site,
                             aes(treatment, mean, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
                width = 0.16, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ site_year, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rolled_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("RNO", "RIM", "RIC")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
  labs(x = "Rolled rye treatment", y = "Remaining mulch biomass (kg/ha)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

mulch_site_year_fig
```

```{r save-figures, eval=FALSE}
# Run this chunk when ready to export publication-quality figures.
dir.create(here("figures"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave(here("figures", "total_mulch_biomass_overall.png"),
       mulch_overall_fig, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(here("figures", "total_mulch_biomass_by_site_year.png"),
       mulch_site_year_fig, width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# Interpretation notes

- Report the interaction test first to describe whether treatment effects
  differ among site-years.
- Prioritize the estimated RIM − RNO difference, confidence interval, and
  adjusted *p*-value. Report RIC − RNO as the other comparison against the
  undisturbed control.
- Distinguish **remaining mulch biomass** from mulch *loss*. Because this is a
  single sampling occasion, the data do not directly quantify loss caused by
  mowing or cultivation.
- The pooled raw SE includes site-year variation; use the model-based contrast
  interval for treatment inference.
- Follow-up analyses can examine 2024 in-row/inter-row mulch distribution and
  associations with weed biomass, accounting for site-year and block.
